request: Employees pick a request topic from presets the organization curates (VPN, Claude, Question, Other for staff; Access, Other for clients), and the screens say Pending / In progress / Completed / Closed

findings.claim: The seed set does not cover the access kind `saas`, so the claim that nothing classifiable before becomes unclassifiable is false.

witness.detail: Seed Data (contracts:231): 'The staff set covers what the retired `accessKind` vocabulary covered, plus the two the request named, so nothing an organization could classify before becomes unclassifiable.' The seeded staff rows (contracts:219-227) are VPN, Claude, Repository, Environment, Server, Admin panel, Documentation, Question, Other. `grep -n "ACCESS_KINDS" -A 10 packages/validation/src/requests.ts` returns eight values: repository, environment, server, vpn, saas, admin_panel, documentation, other. `saas` — 'a seat on a paid tool', the case the contracts' own POST example has to invent a topic for ('Figma seat', contracts:53) — has no seeded topic, and `Other` is seeded as `question` rather than `access`, so the old `other` access is not expressible either.

findings.suggestedFix: Either seed a staff `access` topic for the SaaS case and decide the `type` of `Other` deliberately, or delete the coverage claim and say instead which retired kinds are intentionally dropped.

findings.claim: The design system does export a segmented control, so the stated gap does not exist and the workaround it justifies is unwarranted.

witness.detail: DS gaps (contracts:370): 'No segmented-control primitive | The Staff / Client audience switch | Two `Button`s with an aria-pressed state … | A `SegmentedControl` in `@ds`, adopted by this screen and the requests scope toggle together'. `grep -n Toggle apps/web/src/ds.ts` shows `Toggle` re-exported from `@ds`; `1_DS for dev/components/navigation/Toggle.d.ts:10` reads '/** Pill-shaped segmented control — the day/week/month + light/dark pattern. */' and `Toggle.prompt.md:3` 'Segmented pill toggle.' The requests scope toggle the row proposes to convert already uses the DS `Tabs` primitive (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/page.tsx:321-329).

findings.suggestedFix: Drop the row and draw the audience switch with the existing `Toggle` (or `Tabs`). If the real gap is that `Toggle` forwards no `data-testid` and sets no `aria-pressed`, which is what `request-topics-audience-staff`/`-client` need, state that gap instead — it is a different gap with a different fix.

findings.claim: The catalogue screen is specified twice with two different ordering controls.

witness.detail: Screens (contracts:305-309) draws a drag handle on every row: '│  ⠿  VPN               access                        [ Rename ] [ Archive ]   │', repeated for all five rows. DS gaps (contracts:369) says the opposite ships: 'No drag-handle or reorder list primitive | The catalogue's ordering control | Up and down controls on each row, each issuing one `PATCH` — keyboard-reachable, and no pointer-only interaction'. No implementation draws both, and no case or `data-testid` decides which one a screen must show.

findings.suggestedFix: One control, in both places. If the up/down controls are the decision, redraw the mock with them and add their `data-testid`s to the Required list.

findings.claim: Four integration cases assert audit fields on 'the row' that the declared response shape does not carry, leaving the contract of five routes undecided.

witness.detail: The topic row shape (contracts:34-47) is `id`, `audience`, `type`, `name`, `sortOrder`, `status`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` — and every write route returns it ('`201` with `{ "topic": { … } }`, the row shape above', contracts:56; 'No body. `200` with `{ "topic": { … } }`', contracts:67). TC-02-INT-08 (cases:256-259) expects 'the row carries `archivedAt` and `archivedByAccountId` … After the restore both audit fields are null'; TC-02-INT-01 (cases:156-159) expects 'each with `createdByAccountId` null' from a catalogue read, and 'The seed rows and the `Organization` row share a creation timestamp'; TC-02-INT-09 (cases:273) and TC-02-INT-16 (cases:362-364) assert `archivedAt` too. Two readings, materially different: the routes return three more fields, as the sibling `Client` route does (apps/api/test/clients.spec.ts:171-172 asserts `client.createdByAccountId` and `client.archivedAt` on the response body), or the cases bypass the API and read the table. `Organization.createdAt` is returned by no route at all.

findings.suggestedFix: Decide the response shape once: either add `createdByAccountId`, `archivedAt` and `archivedByAccountId` to the topic row and keep the assertions as body assertions, or say in each case that the audit fields and the creation timestamps are read from the table.

findings.claim: A `topicId` that names no row is a state the requirements never answer, and the two answers in play are 400 and 404.

witness.detail: REQ-02-019 (:186) names two conditions only: 'IF `topicId` names a topic that is archived or belongs to another organization, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL answer `400` with `REQUEST_MESSAGES.topicUnavailable`.' TC-02-INT-13 (cases:320-323) adds a third and demands the same answer: 'Then raise one whose `topicId` is a well-formed id that names no row. … All three answer `400` with the same message and the same body.' The Routes table for that route (contracts:20) declares `404` among its errors, and the route's own code answers 404 for exactly this shape of input on its sibling fields: `if (!assignee || assignee.organizationId !== organizationId) throw new NotFoundException();` (apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts:329) and the same line for the project (:344). An implementer following the requirement and the code's convention returns 404 and fails the case.

findings.suggestedFix: State the rule in REQ-02-019: an id that names no row is answered the same way as an archived one, 400 with `REQUEST_MESSAGES.topicUnavailable` — and say so in the Security section beside the sentence that already covers archived-or-elsewhere.

findings.claim: The history half of REQ-02-028 is asserted by a case that names no selector able to observe it, and the Required list carries none.

witness.detail: REQ-02-028 (:248-250) requires the label map to be read by 'the list, the detail screen, its history entries and the filter control'. TC-02-E2E-04's expected result (cases:483) is 'the history entry for the change reads Closed rather than the stored value', and its Selectors line (cases:484) is 'requests-status-filter, request-row-{id}-status, request-detail-status' — none of which reaches the history panel. The Required data-testid table (contracts:259-287) carries no history id either, so the only way to write the assertion is with `request-detail-history`, which the screen already draws (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/[requestId]/RequestHistory.tsx:48) and which this spec does not name. Today that panel renders the raw value — `${actor} marked it ${event.newValue}` (RequestHistory.tsx:27) — so the clause is a real change with no observer.

findings.suggestedFix: Add `request-detail-history` to the Required list and to TC-02-E2E-04's Selectors, or drop the history clause from REQ-02-028.

findings.claim: The fallback every request that exists today depends on is stated and never observed.

witness.detail: Edge case 8 (contracts:383): 'A request raised before this spec is listed | `topic` is `null`; the row shows the stored `type` as its About value and nothing breaks.' Known Gaps (:306) rests the whole no-backfill decision on it. No case asserts it: TC-02-INT-02 (cases:170-172) asserts columns on the table — 'The request raised earlier still has its `type`, its `topicLabel` and no `topicId`' — not the `topic` member of the response, and no E2E case lists a pre-spec row. Every request now in the database takes this path, and `request-row-{id}-topic` is specified as 'present when the request carries a topic' (contracts:279) with nothing saying what the cell shows when it does not.

findings.suggestedFix: Extend TC-02-INT-02, or add one case, to list a request with no `topicId` and assert `topic` is `null` in the response and that the row renders the stored `type` as its About value.

findings.claim: `sortOrder` has two stated defaults and no value for the first topic of an empty audience.

witness.detail: contracts:56-58: '`sortOrder` is optional and defaults to the highest stored value in that audience plus ten'. The Data Model (contracts:168) gives the column `Int @default(0)`. An audience holding no rows has no highest stored value, and TC-02-INT-03 (cases:180-183) only exercises the seeded case.

findings.suggestedFix: Say what the first topic of an empty audience gets, and note that the column default is never the value a route writes.

findings.claim: The list mock draws a Closed row under a Pending filter.

witness.detail: contracts:335 draws the control as 'Status [ Pending ▾ ]' and contracts:340-341 draws '#9 Which invoice template? … Closed · cancelled' beneath it. REQ-02-028 (:248) maps Pending to `open` only, so that row cannot be in a list filtered to Pending.

findings.suggestedFix: Draw the control as 'Any status' in the mock.

findings.claim: An absence the case asserts has no id to assert it with.

witness.detail: TC-02-E2E-02's expected result (cases:454-455): 'no control for a request kind or an access kind is drawn anywhere in the modal', with Selectors (cases:456-458) naming neither `request-new-type` nor `request-new-access-kind`. The Required list says of those two ids (contracts:292-293) that they 'are **removed** from the new-request modal by REQ-02-022 and appear in no case here'. Both ids exist today (apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/requests/NewRequestModal.tsx), so the assertion is writable — but only by naming ids the spec says no case names, and every other absence in this spec is written as an id marked '(absent)' (cases:495-496, 507-508).

findings.suggestedFix: List them in TC-02-E2E-02's Selectors as '(absent)' and reword the Required-list sentence, or drop the clause from the expected result.

findings.claim: Reordering is specified at four places and observed at none.

witness.detail: The state machine declares 'active | reorder | `sortOrder` is written; `updatedAt` moves' (:274) and 'archived | reorder | `sortOrder` is written' (:278); the PATCH contract accepts `sortOrder` (contracts:62); DS gaps ships up and down controls for it (contracts:369). No case sends `sortOrder` on a PATCH — TC-02-INT-06 renames only — and the Required data-testid list holds no reorder control.

findings.suggestedFix: One integration case that PATCHes `sortOrder` and re-reads the order, and a `data-testid` for the control if it stays in the mock.

findings.claim: Requests spec 01 makes `accessKind` required whenever `type` is `access`; from this spec every new `access` request stores `accessKind` null, so that invariant holds only for rows raised before it.

witness.detail: REQ-02-022 (:210) refuses `accessKind` on the way in and REQ-02-021 (:206) writes `type` from the topic, so a topic of type `access` produces a row with `type = 'access'` and `accessKind = null`. The rule it changes is enforced today in `validateRequestKind` (packages/validation/src/requests.ts:147-152) and documented on the column itself: 'Required when `type = 'access'`, absent otherwise' (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:1134).

findings.suggestedFix: None required — recorded so a person confirms the change was meant.

findings.claim: A request with a `topicLabel` and no `topicId` has two possible serializations.

witness.detail: contracts:97-100: '`topic` is `null` on a request raised before this spec … `topic.status` is read from the catalogue row … and is `null` when the row is gone.' A row that is gone leaves `topicId` null by SetNull (contracts:185) while `topicLabel` stays, which is precisely the state TC-02-INT-02 creates (cases:166-172), and the spec does not say whether `topic` is then `null` (topicId is absent) or an object with a null `id` and `status` (topicLabel is present).

findings.suggestedFix: Name the discriminator once: `topic` is present whenever `topicLabel` is, or whenever `topicId` is.
